source.title: Weakening Neurons: An Input-Output Functionality in Transformers with Outsize Influence
source.authors: Sebastian Gerstner; Hilal AlQuabeh; Kentaro Inui; Hinrich Schütze

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present; no apparent truncation or corruption.
record.tranche_reason: The paper ablates MLP neurons and measures output effects. It reports one case where the effect was indirect and cumulative, relevant to the attribution consequence in V7, but it does not measure downstream-component compensation as described by the other versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports neuron-class ablation effects on entropy, loss, and other metrics, but those results do not track later-component changes or recovery of an original prediction. The specific case of an indirect, cumulative effect bears on V7. Results cited from other studies are not recorded.
record.test_reason: The study classifies GLU neurons by input-output weight cosines and ablates neuron classes to measure output metrics (entropy, loss, attribute rate). It never measures downstream components compensating for an ablation, or recovery of an ablated effect. It cites the Hydra effect and Rushing & Nanda only in related work, on MLP erasure. The Section 7.3 case shows that no single weakening neuron reproduces an indirect effect, while a subset of 8 does. That is a cumulative, distributed effect, not self-repair. It does not show that ablation scores are distorted by compensation, so it does not test V7.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right but incomplete. The main conclusions are: IO functionality is broadly similar across models; IO class predicts activation frequency; and weakening neurons strongly influence model behaviour, including through negative gate values. The indirect, cumulative 8-neuron case is one example whose mechanism is left to future work. The authors do not relate it to self-repair.
record.recipe_differences: The study classifies and ablates MLP neurons by input-output weight relationships, using mean and zero ablation and output metrics. It does not apply the attention-layer or attention-head ablation and compensation measurements in the original sources.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported ablation effects differ by neuron class and activation quadrant; the paper also says mean ablation reveals effects that zero ablation can miss.

fits_no_version.finding: In one OLMo-7B example, no single weakening neuron reproduces the quadrant-(iii) entropy reduction, but a subset of 8 does. The effect is indirect, not via direct logit effect.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Some neuron-class effects are distributed and indirect, so single-neuron ablation can miss them.

fits_no_version.finding: Mean-ablating 526 weakening neurons in OLMo-7B shifts output entropy more than random same-layer neurons or other classes, more often sharpening than flattening.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Late-layer weakening neurons have outsize influence on output entropy relative to their number.

record.peer_reviewed: Proceedings of the 2026 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
record.problems: The indirect, cumulative result is a single example, and the authors leave its mechanism for future work. The main ablation results are shown as plots without numerical values in the text. The ablation experiments measure next-token metrics but do not trace intermediate downstream computations.
record.rows_left_out: Other ablation figures and metrics in Sections 7 and J.2 are not included because they report neuron-class effects on output metrics without measuring downstream compensation, restoration, or attribution consequences.

untested.parts: No attention-layer ablation or compensation measure.
No test of late MLP downregulation of the top token, or of erasure shrinking after upstream ablation.
No compensation ratios, per-prompt variation or overcorrection.
No test of backup heads, copy suppression, LayerNorm rescaling or anti-erasure neurons as repair mechanisms.
Mean and zero ablation are compared only for effect size, not for self-repair.
No comparison of ablation-based importance with direct effect under compensation.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' guess and the V7 'supports' label are removed. Nothing in the study measures compensation. Hydra and Rushing & Nanda appear only as related-work citations on MLP erasure.

versions.untested_parts: No attention-layer ablation or measurement of compensation by later attention layers.
No test of late MLP layers downregulating the maximum-likelihood token, or of that erasure shrinking when earlier components are ablated.
The interventions are on MLP neurons, not attention heads; no full-distribution head-level compensation test.
No prompt-wise compensation or overcorrection analysis.
The paper studies weakening neurons, but does not test backup heads, copy-suppression heads, final LayerNorm rescaling, or anti-erasure neurons as self-repair mechanisms.
Mean and zero neuron ablations are used, but the study does not measure self-repair under either ablation type.
Only one particular example compares a single-neuron effect with a cumulative subset effect; no general ablation-based importance scores or attention-component self-repair are evaluated.

rows.subject: OLMo-7B
rows.operation_detail: Zero-ablation of subsets of weakening neurons, including individual neurons and groups.

conditions.value: Yesterday (21 December) ... the O ...; correct next token is mic (Omicron)
A small subset of 8 weakening neurons produced the effect; no single weakening neuron did so alone

rows.measure: Entropy reduction in the output distribution; comparison of single-neuron and subset ablation effects
rows.value: The observed entropy-reducing effect was indirect and cumulative; the direct effect of weakening neurons did not correspond to the observed effect.
rows.note: A single example indicates that individual-neuron effects did not capture the cumulative subset effect. The paper does not identify this as downstream compensation or establish a general self-repair effect.
rows.check: Linked to V7 in error. The case shows an indirect, cumulative effect of 8 jointly ablated neurons (single neurons insufficient) in one hand-picked example. It contains no measure of compensation by later components, so it cannot show self-repair distorting attribution. The paper does not frame it as self-repair.

rows.subject: OLMo-7B
rows.baseline: Clean run; random neurons from the same layers are shown as a baseline
rows.value: figure only; the text says weakening neurons often flatten the output distribution, but even more often sharpen it, and have a larger effect than other classes or same-layer random neurons.
rows.note: This measures output changes after neuron ablation, not whether later components compensate or restore the original prediction.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked: an ablation effect-size distribution with no compensation measure. The value is figure-only.

reader_labels.reason: The single-neuron effect did not match the indirect, cumulative effect produced by a subset of 8 weakening neurons, consistent with ablation effects failing to capture the broader computation in this case (r1).
